title: Nectarous Venezuelan Pork Stew
description: A winey, molten stew that blends pork shoulder with namul greens and a tropical tamarind-coconut spice mix, ideal for an ovo-vegetarian night.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add pork steaks and sear each side until browned, about 3 minutes per side, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion and garlic until translucent, about 2 minutes.
Stir in cumin, smoked paprika, and tamarind paste, cooking for 30 seconds to release aromas.
Pour in white wine, bring to a simmer, and let it reduce by half, about 5 minutes.
Add coconut milk and soy sauce, stirring to combine, then return pork to the pot.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes, or until pork is tender and juices have thickened.
While pork cooks, blanch the namul greens in boiling water for 1 minute, then shock in ice water and drain.
Stir the blanched namul into the stew during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Serve hot over white rice or with crusty bread, garnish with fresh cilantro if desired.
